name: Hanukkah
description: Light, dedication, and stubborn hope — the Festival of Lights from the Maccabees to the candle in the window.
author: Quips Editorial

quotes.content: Then Judas and his brothers and all the assembly of Israel determined that every year at that season the days of dedication of the altar should be observed with gladness and joy for eight days, beginning with the twenty-fifth day of the month of Chislev.
quotes.notes: The verse that institutes Hanukkah: after the Temple was rededicated in 164 BCE, the festival was fixed at eight days a year beginning on the 25th of Kislev.

quotes.content: Behold, our enemies are crushed; let us go up to cleanse the sanctuary and dedicate it.
quotes.notes: Judas's call to his brothers after the victory at Beth-zur; hanukkah is simply the Hebrew word for the dedication that followed.

quotes.content: It is not on the size of the army that victory in battle depends, but strength comes from Heaven.
quotes.notes: Judas's answer to men who saw how badly they were outnumbered before the battle at Beth-horon.

quotes.content: Let every one who is zealous for the law and supports the covenant come out with me!
quotes.notes: The cry in the village of Modein that began the Maccabean revolt.

quotes.content: It is better for us to die in battle than to see the misfortunes of our nation and of the sanctuary.
quotes.notes: Spoken to his men on the eve of the fight at Emmaus, against a far larger Seleucid force.

quotes.content: Now, my children, show zeal for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
quotes.notes: From Mattathias's deathbed charge to his five sons, among them Judas Maccabeus.

quotes.content: My children, be courageous and grow strong in the law, for by it you will gain honor.
quotes.notes: The closing line of the same charge; the revolt is framed throughout as a defence of practice, not of territory.

quotes.content: Far be it from us to do such a thing as to flee from them. If our time has come, let us die bravely for our brethren, and leave no cause to question our honor.
quotes.notes: Judas's refusal to retreat at Elasa, the battle in which he was killed; the revolt outlived him.

quotes.content: They celebrated it for eight days with rejoicing, in the manner of the feast of booths, remembering how not long before, during the feast of booths, they had been wandering in the mountains and caves like wild animals.
quotes.notes: The oldest surviving explanation of the eight days: the rededication was kept as a delayed Sukkot, which the rebels had spent hiding in the hills.

quotes.content: Each man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to make them afraid.
quotes.notes: The peace that came under Simon, Judas's surviving brother — what the eight days were finally for.

quotes.content: And from that time to this we celebrate this festival, and call it Lights. I suppose the reason was, because this liberty beyond our hopes appeared to us.
quotes.source: Antiquities of the Jews, Book XII, ch. 7, trans. William Whiston
quotes.notes: The first surviving use of 'Festival of Lights' for Hanukkah, written some 230 years after the rededication — and note that Josephus gives liberty, not oil, as the reason.

quotes.content: When the Hasmoneans prevailed against and defeated them, they made search and found only one cruse of oil which lay with the seal of the High Priest, but which contained sufficient for one day's lighting only; yet a miracle was wrought therein and they lit the lamp therewith for eight days.
quotes.notes: The Talmud's own answer to its question 'What is Hanukkah?'; rendered from the standard text of the Babylonian Talmud.

quotes.content: Beth Shammai maintain: On the first day eight lights are lit and thereafter they are gradually reduced; but Beth Hillel say: On the first day one is lit and thereafter they are progressively increased.
quotes.notes: The dispute behind the familiar practice — the law follows Beth Hillel, which is why the menorah grows brighter each night rather than dimmer.

quotes.content: We promote in matters of sanctity but do not reduce.
quotes.notes: The reason given for Beth Hillel's ascending lights; the principle reaches well beyond Hanukkah.

quotes.content: The precept of Hanukkah demands one light for a man and his household.
quotes.notes: The baseline obligation: one flame per night per home satisfies it, and everything past that is embellishment.

quotes.content: It is incumbent to place the Hanukkah lamp by the door of one's house on the outside.
quotes.notes: The rule that makes Hanukkah a public festival — the lights exist to be seen from the street, which the Talmud calls publicizing the miracle.

quotes.content: The mitzvah of kindling Hanukkah lamps is very dear, and a person should be very careful in its observance, in order to publicize the miracle.
quotes.source: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Megillah and Hanukkah 4:12
quotes.notes: Maimonides ranks the Hanukkah lights among the most beloved of the rabbinic commandments.

quotes.content: Even if a person has no resources for food except from charity, he should borrow or sell his garment to purchase oil and lamps and kindle them.
quotes.source: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Megillah and Hanukkah 4:12
quotes.notes: The measure of how seriously the obligation is taken; the same ruling is made for wine at the Passover seder.

quotes.content: If a person has before him only enough for a Shabbat lamp or a Hanukkah lamp, the Shabbat lamp takes precedence, because of peace in the home.
quotes.source: Mishneh Torah, Laws of Megillah and Hanukkah 4:14
quotes.notes: Even the festival's own lights yield to shalom bayit — a quiet household outranks publicizing the miracle.

quotes.content: You delivered the strong into the hands of the weak, the many into the hands of the few, the impure into the hands of the pure, the wicked into the hands of the righteous.
quotes.source: Al HaNissim, added to the Amidah and to Grace after Meals on Hanukkah
quotes.notes: The Hanukkah insertion recited all eight days; the theology of the festival in a single sentence, and notably it never mentions the oil.

quotes.content: These lights are sacred, and we are not permitted to make ordinary use of them, but only to look at them.
quotes.source: Hanerot Halalu, recited after kindling the Hanukkah lights
quotes.notes: Drawn from Talmud, Shabbat 21b-22a: the flames are for contemplation, not for reading or working by.

quotes.content: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who performed miracles for our ancestors in those days, at this season.
quotes.source: She-asa Nissim, the second blessing recited over the Hanukkah lights
quotes.notes: Said each night before kindling; 'in those days, at this season' places whoever is lighting inside the story rather than outside it.

quotes.content: Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
quotes.notes: Read as the haftarah on Shabbat Hanukkah, alongside a vision of a golden lampstand — the tradition's own commentary on its military story.

quotes.content: Weeping may tarry for the night, but joy cometh in the morning.
quotes.notes: Psalm 30 is headed 'A Song at the Dedication of the House' and is recited on each of the eight days.

quotes.content: The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts.
quotes.notes: A favourite Hanukkah text of the commentators: the candle in the window has a counterpart inside the person lighting it.

quotes.content:
Kindle the taper like the steadfast star
Ablaze on evening's forehead o'er the earth,
And add each night a lustre till afar
An eightfold splendor shine above thy hearth.
quotes.notes: The opening stanza, written by the poet whose later sonnet 'The New Colossus' was engraved on the Statue of Liberty.

quotes.content:
Wake, Israel, wake! Recall to-day
The glorious Maccabean rage,
The sire heroic, hoary-gray,
His five-fold lion-lineage.
quotes.notes: Lazarus turns the Maccabees into a summons to her own generation; the 'five-fold lion-lineage' is Mattathias and his five sons.

quotes.content:
Blessed is the match consumed in kindling flame.
Blessed is the flame that burns in the secret fastness of the heart.
quotes.source: 'Blessed is the Match' (1944), trans. Marie Syrkin
quotes.notes: Written in Yugoslavia days before Senesh crossed into occupied Hungary on a rescue mission; she was captured and executed that November, aged 23.

quotes.content: A little light dispels much darkness.
quotes.notes: Attribution is the uncertain axis: the maxim is quoted in the Tanya but is older than it, appearing in earlier midrashic and kabbalistic literature, and the English wording varies with the translator.

quotes.content:
Rock of Ages, let our song
Praise Thy saving power;
Thou amidst the raging foes
Wast our sheltering tower.
quotes.source: 'Rock of Ages,' the English adaptation of Ma'oz Tzur (c. 1880s)
quotes.notes: Attribution is the uncertain axis: the hymn sung in English-speaking synagogues is a free adaptation rather than a translation of the 13th-century Hebrew Ma'oz Tzur, and while it is usually credited to Jastrow and Gottheil, the division of authorship between them is not documented.
